plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic of a single array drawn as a long horizontal strip of equal cells, shaded to mark off four regions. Four italic labels sit above the strip: p over the leftmost cell, i over the fourth cell, j further to the right, and r over the rightmost cell. Three heavy black bars stand between cells as the region boundaries. The four cells from p through i are pale gray; the six cells between the first and second bar are a darker gray; the five cells after the second bar and before the last are white and empty; and the single cell at the right end, under r, is white and holds the italic letter x. Three curly braces beneath the strip label the pale gray stretch as at most x, written with the symbol for less than or equal to followed by x, the dark gray stretch as greater than x, and the white stretch as unrestricted. The shading separates the portion of the array already classified against the pivot from the portion not yet examined. The strip states the invariant holding at the top of each iteration while a subarray is rearranged in place around the pivot value stored at position r.

interactionPlan.concept: At the top of every iteration of PARTITION's loop the subarray is split into four regions — A[p..i] ≤ x, A[i+1..j-1] > x, A[j..r-1] unexamined, and the pivot x at A[r] — and each iteration restores this invariant by either advancing j alone or swapping and advancing both i and j.
elements: Long horizontal strip of equal-width rectangular cells representing the subarray A[p..r]
Italic index labels above the strip: p over the leftmost cell, i over the last pale-gray cell, j over the first unexamined cell, r over the rightmost cell
Three heavy black vertical bars drawn between cells marking the boundaries at i, at j-1/j, and just before r
Pale-gray shaded run of cells from p through i (the ≤ x region)
Darker-gray shaded run of cells from i+1 through j-1 (the > x region)
White unshaded run of cells from j through r-1 (the unrestricted / unexamined region)
Single white cell at the far right under r containing the italic letter x (the pivot)
Three curly braces beneath the strip labelling the regions: '≤ x', '> x', 'unrestricted'
Numeric value drawn inside each cell (element values of the working array)
Highlight ring / arrow on the cell currently at index j being compared
Swap indicator: curved double-headed arrow between cells i and j when a swap occurs
Comparison readout annotation, e.g. 'A[j] = 1 ≤ x = 4'
Frame counter / step caption line showing the note text for the current recorded step
Legend mapping pale gray = ≤ x, dark gray = > x, white = unrestricted, boxed x = pivot

interactions.teaches: That the four-region picture is not decoration but a loop invariant the code must actively maintain: the learner writes the loop and watches the boundaries i and j move exactly as their own comparisons and swaps dictate, and sees the regions break when the logic is wrong.
interactions.label: Implement PARTITION(A, p, r)

interactions.success_check: the returned index q satisfies: every cell in A[p..q-1] is ≤ A[q], A[q] equals the original pivot x, and every cell in A[q+1..r] is > A[q]

interactions.teaches: Why the two branches differ: when A[j] ≤ x the ≤ x region must grow, which requires a swap to evict the > x element sitting at i+1; when A[j] > x the > x region simply absorbs the cell and i never moves.

demo_steps.title: Read the picture before running anything
demo_steps.narration: The strip shows the state at the top of one iteration: pale gray cells are already known ≤ x, dark gray cells are known > x, white cells have not been looked at, and the pivot x sits alone at position r. The bars at i and j are the only things that move.

demo_steps.title: The skip branch: A[j] > x
demo_steps.narration: When the scanned cell is greater than the pivot, nothing is exchanged — j advances by one and the dark gray > x region simply swallows the cell. The i bar and the pale gray region are untouched.

demo_steps.title: The swap branch: A[j] ≤ x
demo_steps.narration: When the scanned cell is at most the pivot, the ≤ x region must grow by one cell, but that cell is currently occupied by a > x value. Incrementing i and swapping A[i] with A[j] moves the small value left and pushes the big value to the far end of the > x region — both bars advance.

demo_steps.title: Write the loop yourself
demo_steps.narration: Implement partition with lessEq, swap, setI and setJ, then replay it frame by frame. Every boundary you see move is one of your own setI/setJ calls; every recolored cell is one of your swaps.

demo_steps.title: Break it on purpose
demo_steps.narration: Load the buggy version that swaps before incrementing i. With invariant checking on, watch a cell greater than x appear inside the pale gray region — the picture stops being true, and the final array is no longer partitioned.

demo_steps.title: Termination: place the pivot
demo_steps.narration: When j reaches r the unrestricted region is empty, so the array is just ≤ x followed by > x followed by the pivot. One final swap of A[i+1] with A[r] drops the pivot exactly on the seam, and i+1 is the returned split point.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The i bar is the frontier of what is known small and the j bar is the frontier of what has been looked at at all; every iteration examines exactly one new cell and the only question is whether that cell forces the small-region frontier to move too — which is precisely what the single swap accomplishes.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw one wide horizontal strip of ~16 equal cells with thin black outlines, centered on a light background. Italic serif labels p, i, j, r sit above the strip aligned to the first cell, the last pale-gray cell, the first white cell, and the last cell respectively. Three thick black vertical bars (much heavier than the cell borders) sit on the cell boundaries at i, before j, and before r. Color runs: pale gray (#e8e8e8) from p to i, medium gray (#a8a8a8) from i+1 to j-1, white from j to r-1, and a white pivot cell under r containing an italic x. Beneath the strip, three thin curly braces span the three runs with centered captions '≤ x', '> x', and 'unrestricted' in serif type. During replay, show the array's numeric values inside cells, ring the cell at j in a strong accent color (orange) when compared, and draw a curved double-headed arc above the strip between cells i and j during a swap. Keep the code editor panel to the left or below with the replay scrubber and a caption line showing the current note(). Invariant-violation cells should get a red hatched fill so a wrong implementation is visually obvious against the intended gray shading.

discrepancies: Typography scale: in the source the index labels (p, i, j, r) and the brace captions (≤ x, > x, unrestricted) are large and dominant; in the render they shrink to ~10–11 effective px because the 640×150 viewBox is letterboxed into a wider container, so the label hierarchy is much weaker than the original.
The pivot glyph 'x' is centred in the last cell, whereas in the source it sits left-aligned/lower-left inside the pivot cell — a cosmetic but visible difference.
The strip is drawn at a fixed 640×150 viewBox and ends up occupying only roughly half of the available container width, leaving large empty margins; the source figure is a full-bleed wide banner.

Braces in the source clearly terminate flush with the heavy bars and the array ends; in the render the '≤ x' brace stops a pixel short of the i-bar and the 'unrestricted' brace stops before the pivot bar, making the spans read slightly narrower than the source.
evaluation.notes: The default schematic reproduces the CLRS partition-invariant strip almost exactly (16 cells, correct pale/dark/white regions, three heavy bars, p/i/j/r labels and three braces), and the interaction suite (demo steps, branch selector, apply-iteration, invariant checking, code workbench with frame playback) is deep and pedagogically on-target; the main weaknesses are undersized label typography relative to the source's bold hierarchy and a figure that renders smaller than the available width.
action_items: Increase the viewBox-relative font sizes (index labels ~22–24, brace captions ~18–20) or reduce the viewBox height so the strip scales up, restoring the source's large, dominant p/i/j/r and ≤ x / > x / unrestricted lettering.
Make the SVG fill the available container width (e.g. widen the viewBox aspect ratio to match the source's ~5:1 banner) so the strip is not letterboxed with large empty margins.
Left-align the pivot 'x' glyph inside the final cell to match the source's placement.
Extend the braces so their endpoints sit flush with the heavy bars and the array ends, as in the source.

feedback.rationale: Concept and interaction structure are correct with no failure modes; remaining issues are purely implementation details (font sizing, viewBox aspect, glyph alignment, brace endpoints) that the generator can fix.

In the trace/run view the picture is re-labelled with numeric cell values and a 'q' label, which departs from the abstract source schematic (acceptable as an extension, but it means the figure only matches the source in step 1 / Schematic mode).
claude-opus-5.notes: Near-exact reproduction of the CLRS partition-invariant strip (16 cells, correct 4/6/5+pivot split, heavy bars at i, j and r, correct braces and p/i/j/r labels, correct grays) backed by a rich and genuinely functional interaction set (demo stepper, branch selector, apply-iteration, invariant checker, code sandbox with replay); the main weaknesses are the small rendered scale caused by an oversized control panel and slightly under-emphasised caption typography.
